transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, what brought me in today is that... I find myself checking things over and over. The same boxes, my lists, the drawers around the condo. I just have to check them multiple times before I can move on with my day. 

The frustrating part is that I know perfectly well I already looked. But I still do it anyway, even when my wife is standing right there, waiting for me to just leave it be so we can go. It's just become a bit of a nuisance, to be honest.
Before you check, do you experience an unwanted thought or fear that something bad might happen if you don’t check?

Well, yes. I keep getting these... nagging thoughts. I'll start worrying that I might have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe I put a tool I need in the wrong box. And even when I tell myself it's highly unlikely, the thought just comes back. It just makes it very hard to settle down until I go look.
About how much time each day do you spend checking?

I couldn't give you an exact number, really. I haven't... I haven't ever timed it. It's usually just a few minutes here and there throughout the day. It's not taking up my whole afternoon or anything, so I'm not exactly sure what it adds up to.
For how long have these recurring worries and checking behaviors been happening?

Well, I'm really not sure, to be honest. I haven't kept track of exactly when it all started. It feels like it just sort of... crept up on me over time. I couldn't give you a specific month or year it began, I just know it's been going on for a while now.
How much do the recurring worries and checking behaviors interfere with your daily life?

Well, it does get in the way. For one, unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it really should. And... I've been putting off my preparation for the library tutoring I do, and even my regular hobbies. It's just that I feel like I can't move on to those other things until everything is verified enough.
